Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 84, verses 1–5:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Inshiqaq (The Splitting Asunder), because it opens with mention of the splitting of the sky, which is among the terrors of the Day of Resurrection.

Among the objectives of the surah

• Describing the scenes of the Hereafter, and pointing to the change that will take place in the world when the Hour arrives, and explaining the difference in the states of creation on that Day: between the people of bliss, who are honored, who take their books in their right hands, and the people of wretchedness, who are humiliated, who take their books from behind their backs.

• Rebuking the polytheists for not believing despite the clarity of the verses of the Qur'an and the brightness of its proofs, and giving them the good news of a painful punishment in the abode of the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim).

[The Tafsir]

When the sky is split open and rent asunder with clouds on the Day of Resurrection, and it obeys its Lord in what He commanded it of splitting, and it is right that it submit to His command. And when the earth is spread out and expanded, and its mountains are leveled on that Day, and it casts out what is in its belly of the dead, and empties itself of them, and submits to its Lord in what He commanded it, and it is right that it submit to His command.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 84, verses 16–19:**

God Most High swears by the reddening of the horizon at sunset, by the night and what it gathers of animals, insects, and creeping things and other creatures, and by the moon when its light is complete, that you, O people, will surely pass through many stages and varied conditions: from a drop of semen, to a clinging clot, to a lump of flesh, to the breathing of the soul into it, to death, to resurrection and gathering. It is not permissible for a created being to swear by anything other than God, and if he did so, he would commit shirk.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 84, verses 20–24:

So what prevents them from believing in Allah and the Last Day, after the signs have been made clear to them? And what is wrong with them that, when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate to Allah, nor submit to what it contains? Indeed, the disposition of those who disbelieve is denial and opposition to the truth. And Allah knows best what they conceal in their breasts of obstinacy, while they know that what the Qur'an brought is true. So give them glad tidings, O Messenger, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for them a painful punishment.
